gloss: fat, rich; oil; eight, eighth, eighty
summary: One spelling for two older roots. The first is fat and richness: the verb is to grow fat (Deu 32:15), שָׁמֵן is fat, rich or robust, of land, food and men (Num 13:20; Jdg 3:29), and שֶׁמֶן is oil, above all olive oil, for food, for the lamp, mixed into the grain offering (Lev 23:13), and poured on priests and kings to set them apart (Exo 30:25; 1Sa 16:13). The second is the number eight: שְׁמֹנֶה “eight”, שְׁמֹנִים “eighty”, and שְׁמִינִי “eighth”, the eighth day on which circumcision, the cleansed man’s offering and the close of חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת fall (Lev 12:3; 14:10; 23:36, 39). Arabic, Ugaritic and Aramaic keep them apart: oil and fat are šmn (Arabic samn, Ugaritic šmn, Aramaic שׁוּמְנָא), eight is ṯmn (Arabic ṯamāniya, Ugaritic ṯmn, Aramaic תְּמָנֵי).

words.summary: Oil, almost always the oil of the olive (שֶׁמֶן זַיִת, Exo 27:20): a staple of the land with grain and wine, the fuel of the lamp, part of the grain offering, and the oil of anointing; and as fat itself, the richness of a hill or a feast. 193 uses, nearly half in Exodus, Leviticus and Numbers.

senses.gloss: oil, olive oil (as produce and food)
senses.definition: The oil pressed from olives: one of the goods of the land with grain and wine, eaten with flour, stored, traded and given.

evidence.note: A land of wheat and barley, vines, figs and pomegranates, “a land of זֵית שֶׁמֶן and honey”: olives of oil.
“You shall tread the olive (זַיִת), but not anoint yourself with שֶׁמֶן”: the oil is what the trodden olive yields.
The widow of Zarephath has only “a handful of flour in the jar and a little שֶׁמֶן in the flask”, to bake a last cake; it does not fail until the rain (17:14, 16).
The prophet’s widow has nothing but a jar of oil; it fills every vessel she borrows, and she sells it to pay her debt (4:6–7).
“Fine flour and honey and שֶׁמֶן you ate.”
Solomon gives Hiram wheat and beaten oil year by year.
Judah and Israel trade wheat, honey, oil and balm with Tyre.
Ephraim makes a covenant with Assyria “and שֶׁמֶן is carried to Egypt”: oil as a gift to buy an ally.
Israel says her lovers give her bread and water, wool and flax, oil and drink.
“He who loves wine and שֶׁמֶן will not be rich.”
Treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; the fool swallows it up.
“Gather wine and summer fruit and oil, and put them in your vessels.”
Yahweh made Jacob suck honey out of the rock “and שֶׁמֶן out of the flinty rock”: plenty from where none could be looked for.
Of Asher: “let him dip his foot in שֶׁמֶן”.
In his prosperity “the rock poured out for me streams of שֶׁמֶן”.
Rehoboam stores food, oil and wine in his fortresses.

senses.definition: Oil poured on, mixed into or spread on the flour of a grain offering, and given by measure with the burnt offerings; left out of the sin offering of the poor and the offering of jealousy.

evidence.note: “Fine flour shall be his offering, and he shall pour שֶׁמֶן on it and put frankincense on it.”
Cakes “mixed with oil” and wafers “anointed with oil”.
The poor man’s sin offering of flour: “he shall put no שֶׁמֶן on it nor frankincense, for it is a sin offering”.
The offering of jealousy: “he shall pour no שֶׁמֶן on it nor put frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy … bringing iniquity to remembrance”.
With the lamb of the עֹמֶר day, “two tenths of fine flour mixed with שֶׁמֶן, an offering by fire to Yahweh”.
The cleansed man’s offering on the eighth day: flour mixed with oil, and a log of oil.
Each leader’s dish and basin “full of fine flour mixed with שֶׁמֶן”.
Flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil with each lamb.
The continual offering: a tenth of an ephah of flour “mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten שֶׁמֶן”.
In Ezekiel’s house, a third of a hin of oil “to moisten the fine flour”.

senses.definition: Pure beaten olive oil brought for the lampstand of the dwelling, to keep a lamp burning continually.

evidence.note: “Pure beaten שֶׁמֶן זַיִת for the light, to make a lamp burn continually.”
The same command repeated in the Law of the appointed times.
“Oil for the light” among the gifts for the dwelling.
The lampstand with “all its oil vessels” (כְּלֵי שַׁמְנָהּ).
Eleazar’s charge: “the oil for the light … and the anointing oil”.

senses.definition: Oil poured on a person or thing to set it apart for Yahweh: the compounded holy anointing oil of the dwelling and its priests, and the oil with which prophets anointed kings.

evidence.note: “You shall make it a שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹדֶשׁ, a perfume compounded … it shall be a holy anointing oil.”
“This shall be a holy anointing oil to me throughout your generations”: not to be poured on a man’s flesh nor copied (30:32).
Moses poured of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head “and anointed him, to sanctify him”.
He anointed the dwelling and all in it, and sanctified them.
The priests may not leave the tent, “for the anointing oil of Yahweh is on you”.
The high priest “on whose head the anointing oil was poured”.
“The crown of the anointing oil of his God is on him.”
The manslayer stays in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest “who was anointed with the holy oil”.
Samuel took a flask of oil and poured it on Saul’s head: “Has not Yahweh anointed you ruler over his inheritance?”
Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed David, “and the spirit of Yahweh came upon David from that day forward”.
Zadok took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon.
The prophet’s servant poured the oil on Jehu’s head: “I have anointed you king over the people of Yahweh.”
“I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.”
Brothers dwelling together are like the good oil on the head, running down on Aaron’s beard.
Jacob poured oil on the top of the stone he set up at Bethel.

senses.gloss: oil for the head and body: refreshment, joy
senses.definition: Oil rubbed on the head or skin to make the face shine, a mark of gladness and well-being; withheld in mourning, and given in place of mourning.

evidence.note: Wine that gladdens man’s heart, “to make his face shine with שֶׁמֶן”, and bread that strengthens it.
“Pretend to be a mourner … and do not anoint yourself with שֶׁמֶן”: oil is what mourners go without.
To give the mourners of Zion beauty for ashes, “שֶׁמֶן שָׂשׂוֹן instead of mourning”: oil of joy set against mourning.
“You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with שֶׁמֶן שָׂשׂוֹן above your fellows.” Quoted of the Son at Heb 1:9.
“Therefore God, your God, anointed you with the oil of gladness (ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως) above your fellows”, said to the Son.
Before his enemies “you anoint my head with שֶׁמֶן; my cup runs over”.
“I am anointed with fresh oil.”
“Let your garments be always white, and let your head lack no שֶׁמֶן.”
Those at ease in Zion “anoint themselves with the best שְׁמָנִים, but are not grieved for the ruin of Joseph”.
Under the curse: olive trees throughout the land, “but you shall not anoint yourself with שֶׁמֶן”.
The rebuke of the righteous is “oil for the head”, which my head will not refuse.
Yahweh washed the foundling and anointed her with oil.
“My head with oil (ἐλαίῳ) you did not anoint”: the host’s courtesy to a guest.

senses.definition: Oil applied to soften and soothe wounds.

evidence.note: Wounds and bruises and fresh sores, “not pressed out, nor bound up, nor softened with שֶׁמֶן”.
The Samaritan bound up the man’s wounds, “pouring on oil (ἔλαιον) and wine”.
The elders pray over the sick, “anointing him with oil (ἐλαίῳ) in the name of the Lord”.

senses.definition: Oil made fragrant with spices: a perfume, prized for its scent, and so a likeness for a good name.

evidence.note: “Your שְׁמָנִים are good for fragrance; your name is שֶׁמֶן poured out.”
“A good name (שֵׁם) is better than good oil (שֶׁמֶן)”: the play on the two words.
Dead flies make the perfumer’s oil stink.
“Oil and perfume rejoice the heart.”
“The fragrance of your oils than all spices.”
Six months with oil of myrrh.
Hezekiah shows the Babylonians his spices and “the good oil”.
“You went to the king with שֶׁמֶן and multiplied your perfumes”: oil as a gift in Israel’s courting of foreign powers.

senses.definition: In comparisons, the smoothness of oil for flattering speech, and its soaking in for what enters a man.

evidence.note: “His words were softer than שֶׁמֶן, yet they were drawn swords.”
The lips of the strange woman drip honey, “and her palate is smoother than שֶׁמֶן”, but her end is bitter (5:4).
Cursing came into his body like water, “and like שֶׁמֶן into his bones”.

senses.definition: Fat itself rather than oil: the richness of fertile ground and of a feast; and with מִן, a body wasted from its fat.

evidence.note: The vineyard was “on a horn, a son of שֶׁמֶן”: a very fertile hill.
Samaria, the crown of pride “on the head of the valley of שְׁמָנִים”: the rich valley.
On this mountain Yahweh of hosts will make for all peoples “a feast of שְׁמָנִים, a feast of wines on the lees, שְׁמָנִים full of marrow”: rich food.
“My knees are weak from fasting, and my flesh is lean מִשָּׁמֶן”: wasted, without fat.
The yoke “shall be destroyed מִפְּנֵי שָׁמֶן”: probably “because of fatness”, the ox grown too fat for the yoke, but the image is not certain.

senses.definition: A tree named for its oil, distinct from the olive: its branches were cut for booths, its wood made the cherubim and doors of Solomon’s house, and it is planted in the wilderness in Isaiah. Which tree it is cannot be fixed from the text.

evidence.note: For סֻכּוֹת: “olive branches (עֲלֵי זַיִת) and branches of עֵץ שֶׁמֶן, myrtle, palm and leafy trees”: named beside the olive, so not the olive.
Two cherubim of עֲצֵי שֶׁמֶן, ten cubits high.
The doors of the inner room.
“I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle and the עֵץ שָׁמֶן.”

evidence.locator: Lev.23.13, בַּשֶּׁמֶן → ἐν ἐλαίῳ; Psa.45.8, שֶׁמֶן → ἔλαιον; ἔλαιον renders שֶׁמֶן ×150

evidence.note: Quotes Psa 45:8: “God, your God, anointed you with ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως above your fellows.”
Oil and wine poured on wounds (Isa 1:6).
The twelve anointed many sick with oil and healed them.
The foolish virgins took no oil for their lamps (Exo 27:20).
Oil on the head set beside μύρον on the feet.
A debt of a hundred baths of oil.
“Do not harm the oil and the wine.”

evidence.locator: Sng.1.3, שֶׁמֶן → μύρον, שְׁמָנֶיךָ → μύρων; Amo.6.6 and Pro.27.9 the same

evidence.note: “My head with oil you did not anoint, but she has anointed my feet with μύρῳ.”
Mary anoints Jesus’ feet with a pound of costly μύρου, and the house is filled with its fragrance.
“In pouring this μύρον on my body she did it for my burial.”

parallels.note: Wine and oil, the goods of the land and of gladness, often with grain (דָּגָן, תִּירוֹשׁ, יִצְהָר being the commoner triad).
Frankincense, put with oil on the grain offering, and left off with it from the sin offering and the offering of jealousy.
A good name set beside good oil, in a play on the sounds.

opposites.note: Mourning: oil of joy given in place of it, and oil left off by a mourner.

phrases.gloss: mixed with oil (of flour for the grain offering)

words.summary: Fat: of land and pasture, rich and fertile; of food, rich; of men and beasts, well fed and strong. Ten uses.

senses.gloss: fat, rich, fertile (of land and food)
senses.definition: Of land or pasture, rich and fruitful, the opposite of lean; of bread and food, rich.

evidence.note: The spies are to see “whether the land is שְׁמֵנָה or lean (רָזָה)”.
They took fortified cities and “a fat land (אֲדָמָה שְׁמֵנָה)”, houses full of good things, and grew fat.
“The wide and fat land that you gave them.”
“They found fat and good pasture, and the land was wide and quiet.”
Yahweh will feed his flock “in a fat pasture on the mountains of Israel”.
“Out of Asher his bread shall be שְׁמֵנָה, and he shall yield royal dainties.”
Bread of the ground’s increase “shall be דָשֵׁן וְשָׁמֵן”: rich and fat.
The Chaldean sacrifices to his net, “because by them his portion is שָׁמֵן and his food rich”.

senses.gloss: robust, well fed (of men and flocks)
senses.definition: Of men, stout and strong; of sheep, fat and strong, and in Ezekiel the strong of the flock who push the weak aside.

evidence.note: Ten thousand men of Moab, “every one שָׁמֵן and every one a man of valour, and not one escaped”.
“The fat (הַשְּׁמֵנָה) and the strong (הַחֲזָקָה) I will destroy; I will feed them with justice”: those who butted the weak (34:20–21).

evidence.locator: Gen.49.20, שְׁמֵנָה → πίων; Ezk.34.14 → πίονι; πίων renders שָׁמֵן ×4; not used in the New Testament

parallels.note: Strong, beside fat, of the flock’s oppressors.

words.summary: To grow fat, and causative to make fat. Five uses, every one of a people grown fat on Yahweh’s goodness and turned from him, or a heart made fat so that it cannot understand.

senses.definition: To become fat, well fed; in each use, the fatness of a people who have grown proud and forsaken their God or the poor.

evidence.note: “Jeshurun grew fat (וַיִּשְׁמַן) and kicked; you grew fat (שָׁמַנְתָּ), you grew thick, you were gorged; and he forsook God who made him.”
“They have grown fat (שָׁמְנוּ), they are sleek … they do not judge the cause of the fatherless.”

senses.definition: To make a heart fat: to make it dull and unfeeling, so that it neither understands nor turns.

evidence.note: “Make the heart of this people fat (הַשְׁמֵן), make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, lest they see … and understand with their heart, and turn and be healed.”
Jesus quotes Isa 6:10 of those who hear his parables and do not understand: “the heart of this people has grown fat (ἐπαχύνθη)”.
Paul quotes it of the Jews in Rome who would not believe.
John gives the sense: “he has hardened (πεπώρωκεν) their heart”.

senses.definition: Intransitive, as the qal: to grow fat.

evidence.note: “They ate and were filled and grew fat (וַיַּשְׁמִינוּ) and delighted themselves in your great goodness”; and then “they rebelled against you” (9:26).

greek.gloss: make fat, thick; (of the heart) make dull

evidence.locator: Deu.32.15, עָבִיתָ → ἐπαχύνθη beside שָׁמַנְתָּ → ἐλιπάνθη; at Isa.6.10 the Greek reads ἐπαχύνθη ἡ καρδία, but MACULA leaves הַשְׁמֵן unaligned

evidence.note: Quotes Isa 6:10: “the heart of this people ἐπαχύνθη”.

parallels.note: Grow thick, beside grow fat, of Jeshurun.
Be sleek, beside grow fat, of the wicked in Judah.
Make heavy (the ears), beside make fat (the heart).

words.gloss: fatness; the fat ones, the stoutest; the richest places
words.summary: Fatness of the body, and in the plural the fat ones of a people, its strongest men, or the rich parts of a land. Four uses certainly this word (Isa 10:16; 17:4; Psa 78:31; Dan 11:24); Gen 27:28 and 39 may be it or מִן with שָׁמָן.

senses.definition: The fat of the flesh, and the fat, that is the strongest, men of a people, whom God strikes with leanness or death.

evidence.note: “The glory of Jacob will be brought low, and the fatness (מִשְׁמַן) of his flesh will grow lean (יֵרָזֶה).”
Yahweh of hosts “will send among his fat ones (מִשְׁמַנָּיו) leanness (רָזוֹן)”: against the Assyrian’s army.
God’s anger rose and “he slew the fattest of them (בְּמִשְׁמַנֵּיהֶם) and struck down the chosen men of Israel”: in parallel with בַּחוּרִים.

senses.definition: In the plural, the rich, fertile parts of a province.

evidence.note: The king of the north “will enter peaceably into the richest places (מִשְׁמַנֵּי) of the province” and scatter plunder.

parallels.note: Chosen young men, beside the fattest.

opposites.note: Leanness, sent among the fat ones; and the verb רָזָה, the fatness of flesh grown lean.

words.summary: Only in the plural construct after מִן, “the fatness of the earth”, in Isaac’s blessings of Jacob and Esau; the spelling מִשְׁמַנֵּי may also be read as מִשְׁמָן.

senses.definition: The richness of fertile land, set beside the dew of heaven as what makes a land yield.

evidence.note: “God give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth (מִשְׁמַנֵּי הָאָרֶץ), and plenty of grain and new wine.”
To Esau: “Your dwelling shall be away from the fatness of the earth and away from the dew of heaven above.”

evidence.locator: Gen.27.39, מִשְׁמַנֵּי → ἀπὸ τῆς πιότητος; elsewhere πιότης renders דֶּשֶׁן

evidence.note: The wild olive grafted in becomes partaker “of the root and of the fatness (πιότητος) of the olive”; the Peshitta has שֻׁומְנָא of this root.

parallels.note: The dew of heaven, beside the fatness of the earth.

words.summary: Once, in the plural: the rich food of a feast day.

senses.definition: Fat, rich dishes, eaten in rejoicing and shared with those who have none.

evidence.note: On the first day of the seventh month, after the reading of the law: “Go, eat מַשְׁמַנִּים and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for the day is holy to our Lord.”

evidence.locator: Neh.8.10 (2 Esdras 18:10), מַשְׁמַנִּים → λιπάσματα; not used in the New Testament

parallels.note: Sweet drinks, beside the rich food.

words.summary: Once, and uncertain. If it is of this root, it is “the robust” or “the well fed”: among the vigorous Israel is like the dead, as at noon it stumbles as at dusk. The parallel favours that reading, but no cognate or second use confirms it, and the link to the root rests on the form alone.

senses.definition: Probably those who are strong and well fed, set against “the dead” as noon is set against dusk in the line before.

evidence.note: “We grope for the wall like the blind … we stumble at noon as in the twilight, בָּאַשְׁמַנִּים like the dead”: two contrasts, noon and dusk, the robust and the dead.

words.gloss: eight; (with עָשָׂר) eighteen; (with hundreds, thousands) eight hundred, eight thousand
words.summary: Feminine שְׁמֹנֶה, masculine שְׁמֹנָה (construct שְׁמֹנַת), with the same reversal of gender as the other numbers from three to ten. 109 uses, most of them in the genealogies, reigns and census lists.

senses.definition: The number eight.

evidence.note: “A son of eight days (בֶּן־שְׁמֹנַת יָמִים) shall be circumcised among you, every male”: the eighth day of Lev 12:3 counted from birth.
Abraham circumcised Isaac “a son of eight days”.
Jesse “had eight sons”, of whom David was the youngest.
“These eight Milcah bore to Nahor.”
Ishmael escaped with eight men.
Eight steps up to the gate of the inner court.
They sanctified the house of Yahweh “in eight days”.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

senses.gloss: seven, and eight: enough and more
senses.definition: After seven, the number rises by one to say “as many as are needed, and more”.

evidence.note: When Assyria comes, “we will raise against him seven shepherds and eight princes of men”.
“Give a portion to seven, and also to eight, for you do not know what evil will be on the earth.”

senses.definition: In compound numbers: with עָשָׂר or עֶשְׂרֵה eighteen, with מֵאוֹת eight hundred, with אֲלָפִים eight thousand, and in longer sums.

evidence.note: Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
In the eighteenth year of Josiah, the book of the law was found; his Passover was kept in the same year (23:23).
“The days of Adam after he fathered Seth were eight hundred years.”
Abram’s 318 trained men.
8,600 Kohathites keeping the charge of the holy place.
Eighteen thousand of Israel destroyed on the second day.

evidence.locator: Gen.17.12, שְׁמֹנַת יָמִים → ὀκτὼ ἡμερῶν; ὀκτώ renders שְׁמֹנֶה ×34

evidence.note: “When eight days were fulfilled to circumcise him, his name was called Jesus”: Gen 17:12 and Lev 12:3 kept.
In the ark “a few, that is eight souls, were saved through water”.
“After eight days” Jesus stood among the disciples again, Thomas with them.
About eight days after the saying, the transfiguration.
Aeneas, bedridden eight years.
A daughter of Abraham bound by the adversary eighteen years.

words.summary: The plural of eight, as the tens are formed: eighty, alone or in larger numbers. 38 uses.

senses.definition: The number eighty, of years, men and money.

evidence.note: “Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.”
“The days of our years are seventy years, or if by strength eighty years; yet their pride is labour and sorrow.”
Barzillai: “I am this day eighty years old; can I discern between good and bad?”
The land had rest eighty years.
“In the four hundred and eightieth year” after the exodus Solomon began the house of Yahweh.
The angel of Yahweh struck 185,000 in the camp of Assyria.
Methuselah lived 187 years and fathered Lamech.

evidence.locator: Exo.7.7, שְׁמֹנִים → ὀγδοήκοντα; ὀγδοήκοντα renders it ×28

evidence.note: Anna, a widow of eighty-four years, who did not leave the temple.
“Take your bill and write eighty.”

words.summary: The ordinal of eight, feminine שְׁמִינִית. Most of its uses are “the eighth day”, the day after a seven-day period, on which what the seven days prepared is brought before Yahweh: the circumcision of a son, the cleansed man’s offering, the priests’ first service, the closing assembly of חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת.

senses.definition: The day after a completed seven: a child’s or a young animal’s seven days with its mother, seven days of consecration, uncleanness or a feast; on it the child is circumcised, the animal may be offered, the cleansed are received and the priests begin.

evidence.note: “On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.”
A calf, lamb or kid “shall be seven days under its mother, and from the eighth day and on it shall be accepted” as an offering.
The firstborn of ox and sheep: seven days with its dam, “on the eighth day you shall give it to me”.
After the seven days of consecration (8:33), “on the eighth day” Moses called Aaron and his sons, they offered, and the glory of Yahweh appeared to all the people (9:23–24).
After seven days of covering the altar, “on the eighth day and onward the priests shall make your burnt offerings … and I will accept you”.
The cleansed leper, after seven days outside his tent, brings his offering on the eighth day.
So too the man with a discharge.
And the woman.
The Nazirite defiled by a death, on the eighth day.
After the seven days of סֻכּוֹת, “on the eighth day there shall be a holy convocation for you … it is an עֲצֶרֶת; you shall do no servile work”.
“On the first day a שַׁבָּתוֹן, and on the eighth day a שַׁבָּתוֹן.”
“On the eighth day you shall have an עֲצֶרֶת”, with its own offerings.
They kept the feast seven days, “and on the eighth day an עֲצֶרֶת, according to the ordinance”.
At the dedication of Solomon’s house: “on the eighth day they made an עֲצֶרֶת”.
On the eighth day Solomon sent the people away, glad of heart.
On the eighth day of the leaders’ offerings, Manasseh.

senses.definition: The eighth in any other sequence: the month Bul, the eighth year of a reign or of the land’s sabbath cycle, the eighth son or division.

evidence.note: “In the month Bul, which is the eighth month”, the house was finished.
Jeroboam ordained a feast “in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that is in Judah”, a month later than Yahweh’s seventh (Lev 23:34).
“In the month which he had devised of his own heart.”
“In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius” the word came to Zechariah.
After the sabbath year: “you shall sow in the eighth year and eat of the old produce until the ninth year”.
Peullethai, the eighth son of Obed-edom, “for God blessed him”.

doctrine.statement: The holy anointing oil set apart the dwelling and its priests (Exo 30:25–31; Lev 8:10–12), and Yahweh’s prophets poured oil on the kings he chose: “has not Yahweh anointed you?” (1Sa 10:1). When Samuel anointed David “the spirit of Yahweh came upon David from that day forward” (1Sa 16:13), and Yahweh says “with my holy oil I have anointed him” (Psa 89:21). The king of Psa 45 is anointed by “God, your God” with “the oil of gladness above your fellows” because he loved righteousness (Psa 45:8), and Hebrews says this to the Son (Heb 1:9). The one whom Yahweh anoints in Isa 61 gives mourners “the oil of joy for mourning” (Isa 61:3); Jesus read that passage and said “today this scripture is fulfilled” (Luk 4:18–21), and Peter says “God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with holy spirit and with power” (Act 10:38). From the verses: the oil marked those God chose and set apart for his service, and in David it went with the gift of God’s spirit; the Son was anointed by his God, not with oil from a horn but with the spirit it stood for, because of his righteousness.

Every use of the verb is a warning. Moses foretold that “Jeshurun grew fat and kicked … and forsook God who made him” (Deu 32:15); the Levites confess that in the good land Israel “ate and were filled and grew fat … and rebelled against you” (Neh 9:25–26); Jeremiah says the wicked “have grown fat … they do not judge the cause of the fatherless” (Jer 5:28). Ezekiel’s fat and strong sheep are those who pushed the weak aside, and Yahweh will destroy them (Ezk 34:16, 20–21). Yahweh sent Isaiah to “make the heart of this people fat … lest they understand with their heart, and turn” (Isa 6:10), and Jesus and Paul quote the verse of those who heard and would not understand (Mat 13:15; Act 28:27), John saying “he has hardened their heart” (Jhn 12:40). From the verses: the plenty God gives is good (Gen 27:28; Neh 9:25), but a people grown fat on it forget the giver and the poor, and a heart grown fat is one that can no longer hear him.

The law puts a set of seven days before many things and acts on the eighth: a son is circumcised on the eighth day (Lev 12:3; Gen 17:12); a young animal is seven days with its mother and accepted from the eighth (Lev 22:27); the priests are consecrated seven days and on the eighth begin, and the glory of Yahweh appears (Lev 8:33; 9:1, 23–24); the cleansed man waits seven days and on the eighth brings his offering (Lev 14:8–10); in Ezekiel’s house the altar is covered seven days and “on the eighth day and onward … I will accept you” (Ezk 43:26–27); and after the seven days of סֻכּוֹת the eighth day is a holy convocation and an עֲצֶרֶת (Lev 23:36, 39). The New Testament records the eighth-day circumcision of John and of Jesus (Luk 1:59; 2:21) and Paul’s own (Php 3:5). From the verses: in the law the eighth day is the day on which what seven days have made ready is received before Yahweh. Scripture does not itself draw a further meaning from the number, and none is given here.

Yahweh names his feasts “the appointed times of Yahweh … these are my appointed times” (Lev 23:2), and sets סֻכּוֹת on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (Lev 23:34). Jeroboam kept a feast “in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that is in Judah”, at Bethel, before calves he had made, “in the month which he had devised of his own heart” (1Ki 12:28–33). From the verses: a feast like Yahweh’s, moved to a month of man’s choosing and kept before gods of man’s making, was not Yahweh’s feast; the times are his to appoint.

“On this mountain Yahweh of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of שְׁמָנִים … and he will swallow up death for ever, and the Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from all faces” (Isa 25:6–8). Paul says “death is swallowed up in victory” will come to pass when the dead are raised incorruptible (1Co 15:54), and John hears that God will wipe every tear and death will be no more (Rev 21:4). Jesus speaks of many who will come from east and west and recline with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom (Mat 8:11), and of drinking the fruit of the vine new in his Father’s kingdom (Mat 26:29). From the verses: the rich feast of Isa 25 is set on Zion, for all peoples, in the day when death is swallowed up, that is, at the resurrection and the coming of the kingdom.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Leviticus 23 (שֶׁמֶן, 23:13; שְׁמִינִי, 23:36, 39); Numbers 10 has no word of this root. Root key שמנ as the database keys it (BDB v.eb, v.ec). Two older roots in one spelling: oil and fat are šmn (Arabic s, Ugaritic š, Aramaic ש), eight is ṯmn (Arabic ṯ, Ugaritic ṯ, Sabaic ṯ, Aramaic ת); Akkadian (šamnu against samāne) and Phoenician (šmn for both) do not keep š and ṯ apart, so their cognates carry no sounds. No word of either root is known to draw on the other. BDB keys v.eb.ac (שָׁמָן), v.eb.af (מִשְׁמָן) and v.eb.ag (מַשְׁמָן) each count the same seven tokens (Gen 27:28, 39; Isa 10:16; 17:4; Psa 78:31; Dan 11:24; Neh 8:10), because the database files them by spelling, so each word’s use count is too high; by form, Gen 27:28, 39 are שָׁמָן or מִשְׁמָן, Isa 10:16; 17:4; Psa 78:31; Dan 11:24 are מִשְׁמָן, and Neh 8:10 is מַשְׁמָן. Zero-token cross-reference keys v.ec.aa, v.ec.ae, a.gf.af and m.dw.ak are left out. Not written: the name מִשְׁמַנָּה (Mishmannah, 1Ch 12:11, BDB v.eb.ah), which belongs in names/ and was outside this task. Peshitta: SEDRA root 1887 שמנ (3240 שׁוּמְנָא, 3241 שְׁמִינָא, 3242 שְׁמֵן) and root תמנא (3409–3412); the Peshitta’s oil is מְשַׁחָא (root משח), not this root, so ἔλαιον verses are not cited for the Syriac. Lemma pointings for the Syriac are taken from the Peshitta’s forms (שֻׁומְנָא, שַׁמִּין, תְּמָנְיָא); check against Payne Smith. Isa 6:10 הַשְׁמֵן is not aligned in MACULA, so παχύνω rests on the New Testament quotations; the LXX locator says so. Isa 10:27 (מִפְּנֵי־שָׁמֶן) is kept under “fatness” as the likeliest reading, flagged uncertain. אַשְׁמַנִּים (Isa 59:10) is kept under the root on the strength of the parallel only. Segert pp. 53, 202, 204, Biella pp. 545–546 and Krahmalkov p. 469 were read from OCR or text layers only; check the page images. Ge’ez is from Wiktionary and Anderson–Moser only; check Dillmann and Leslau for ሰማኒ and for any Ge’ez reflex of šmn (none found). Akkadian šummunu “be oiled” (Oracc asbp x000025510) is a verb from šamnu “oil” and does not match the Hebrew verb’s “grow fat”; not entered. Open questions: (1) the sense split of שֶׁמֶן (nine senses) may be finer than needed; (2) the musical עַל־הַשְּׁמִינִית left unexplained; (3) Ezk 34:16 follows the Masoretic אַשְׁמִיד “destroy”.
